A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian/RMT and inverse-Ising research. All 23 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, equations and figures, are readable and support matching retained and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-model training simulations, inverse-Ising experiments and covariance analyses of real datasets, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds generation-metric comparisons, alternative-spectrum experiments, eigenvalue-fitting examples and a larger Ising-lattice experiment.

M1.justification: The stated Gaussian update changes: v1's Eqs. (3) and (33) include Lambda_ij=1-delta_ij/2, whereas v2's Eqs. (3) and (49) omit it under nonsymmetric perturbations. Appendix A explains the corresponding diagonal learning-rate compensation. This revises reported update weighting; the shrinkage, mode-fitting and Ising procedures remain.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds Gaussian training scenarios using a dominant-plus-bulk uniform spectrum and MNIST/HGD-derived population spectra. MNIST and HGD already appeared in v1's covariance analyses; the expansion concerns the population distributions used for Gaussian training, while the principal tasks and domains remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ML, population-eigenvalue correction, L2 and spectral-L1 regularization, RMT shrinkage and empirical mode fitting for Gaussian models, and ML, optimal stopping, L2 and mode fitting for Ising models. The new score-matching/NTK discussion introduces no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds Wasserstein-based generation and early-stopping evaluation and a 32x32 Ising experiment alongside the retained 8x8 experiment. The regularization comparison changes its finite-size grid from N={50,100,300,500} to {100,200,300} (v1 Fig. 11; v2 Fig. 16). New spectrum experiments also specify filtering cutoffs, substantially expanding the evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial sensitivity checks concerning generation-quality metrics, alternative population spectra and Ising lattice size (Appendices E–F and Fig. 20). Figure 18 additionally examines intermediate eigenvalue extrapolations. These extend the retained initialization, eigenbasis and regularization analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten random downsamplings per sample size for eigenmode fitting (v1 Appendix E.2; v2 Appendix H.2). Figure 18 repeats this averaging practice. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: New results include Wasserstein minima tracking likelihood-optimal stopping (Fig. 12), training trajectories under three additional spectra (Figs. 13–15), direct eigenvalue-fitting examples (Fig. 18), and larger-lattice Ising errors (Fig. 20). Finite-size regularization curves are also replaced with the revised size grid. These expand the findings without establishing same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: New Section 7 develops score-matching, NTK/RKHS dynamics and parameter-sample duality for generic EBMs, beyond v1's Gaussian and approximate Ising analyses. Appendix A derives the projected gradient and corrects the symmetry assumptions required for independent eigenmode evolution. The existing RMT derivations are largely retained.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and discussion add a core contribution: generalizing the framework to arbitrary EBMs through NTK dynamics of the score under score matching. v1 primarily establishes the Gaussian framework and its approximate pairwise-binary extension, leaving broader extensions as future work.

C2.justification: Appendix A now qualifies exact mode decoupling under symmetric parameter perturbations, despite unchanged fixed points. Sections 7–8 make the broader extension conditional on kernel/lazy-regime reasoning and acknowledge its need for experimental investigation. The Wasserstein analysis also qualifies the earlier covariance-based assessment of generation quality.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new synthetic spectrum construction, MNIST and HGD filtering thresholds of 10^-6 and 10^-12, and the larger Ising experiment's size and learning rate. Appendix A explains diagonal-rate compensation, and Fig. 18 illustrates the existing fitting procedure. These are focused additions to technical documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused connections to score matching, NTKs, lazy training and kernel interpretations of deep learning through Hyvarinen–Dayan, Jacot, Chizat, Belkin and Hastie references. Delon and Magnus–Neudecker support the metric and gradient additions. The existing EBM, RMT and GCV positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes population/sample notation, edits wording and author information, inserts the theoretical extension and new appendix sections, and adds an impact statement. Most existing paragraphs and the main narrative sequence are retained, so the scientific additions do not amount to wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The graphical presentation expands substantially with symmetry, metric/spectrum, eigenmode-fitting and larger-lattice displays. Figure 12 redisplays Fig. 3's existing measures alongside Wasserstein results. Retained figures are renumbered or relocated, and the regularization comparison is redrawn with revised curves and legends.

improvement.justification: The spectrum, metric and lattice-size checks, together with corrected symmetry assumptions, strengthen v1's evidence. However, the new generic-EBM contribution has unresolved mathematical inconsistencies: Eq. (17) reverses the forcing sign in Eq. (16), and the Gaussian ODE preceding Eq. (14) does not yield its stated solution. The PDFs do not establish whether these are local mistakes or materially undermine the extension, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
